name: Vitralis
description: Vitralis is a serotonergic and visual cortex amplifier that dramatically increases the resolution and saturation of sensory input without inducing hallucinations. Colors become geometrically precise and emotionally overwhelming, sound textures become physically palpable, and taste acquires a narrative quality — users report meals feeling 'like stories.' It is the premier 'clean' recreational compound for people who want intensity without distortion.
effects: Extreme color saturation and visual acuity
Music perceived as three-dimensional and emotionally overwhelming
Time dilation — minutes feel spacious and full
side_effects: Sensory overload in loud or chaotic environments
Temporary photosensitivity after the dose ends
Emotional vulnerability — beauty can trigger intense weeping
Post-experience 'gray day' — colors seem muted for 24-48 hours afterward
cultural_context: Vitralis is deeply embedded in GLMZ's underground art scene. Gallery openings in Tier 3 districts are planned around it — attendees dose together before entering. Among Tier 2 workers, it's a weekend ritual, a way of making the city beautiful again after a week of gray. Critics argue that art is now designed to be experienced on Vitralis rather than sober, creating a feedback loop that has changed aesthetic culture entirely.
story_hooks: A famous GLMZ muralist has been secretly designing her pieces with embedded visual triggers that are only perceivable on Vitralis — the hidden images form a message that someone very powerful wants suppressed
The newest Vitralis batch from Novafold causes users to see a consistent visual anomaly — a figure standing at the edge of their vision — and reports are multiplying across the city

A Tier 2 family's teenage son has been taking Vitralis daily for three months, and the post-experience gray days have accumulated into a permanent perceptual deficit — his parents want to sue Novafold, but the company has buried the clinical data
